cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Secrets Have Value
cards.instruction: Price every fact, introduction, warning, and confession as something that must be traded for equal value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll tell you why I took Mum's spare key if you admit something that could get you grounded too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. That's a weekend. This key is a month. Have you got anything bigger?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I lent her car to Jamie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A month each, then. I used the key to let Jamie move into her flat.

mechanism: A judges the punishment value of confessions and releases the key secret only after approving an equal-risk payment.
confusable: Unlike a trust test, A prices the disclosed fact by equal expected cost rather than whether B can keep it.
comparison: Family grounding stakes differ from workplace information and source introductions.
seedUse: The seed already rejects a low-value confession and announces parity before disclosure, enacting S01 evaluative authority.
